title: Italy and Spain Extend Reciprocal Schengen Border Checks a Third Time
detail: Italy's Interior Ministry, led by Matteo Piantedosi, extended its suspension of Schengen free movement with Spain by another roughly two weeks, through around Sep 30, citing 'high internal security risks' and the possibility of terrorist infiltration linked to the Ceuta crisis. Spain's Interior Ministry responded within hours with a reciprocal 15-day extension of checks on air and sea arrivals from Italy, pushing its own measure to Oct 8. Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares called Rome's decision 'absurd, useless and a disgrace,' saying there is 'no risk or threat to the integrity of the Schengen area arising from Ceuta and Melilla' and accusing Italy of undermining EU solidarity, pointing to Spain's 2023 acceptance of migrants diverted from Lampedusa.

media.caption: Spain extends border checks on Italian arrivals to Oct 8 after Rome's third extension

title: Sánchez's 10,000-Place Target Exposes Contradictions in Government's Own Return Figures
detail: Analysis published a day after Sánchez's 10,000-reception-place announcement noted it sits awkwardly against the government's own claims that roughly 90% of the ~70,000 arrivals were returned to Morocco within 72 hours and that 200 migrants are voluntarily returning daily. Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres' own figures show 5,482 voluntary returns since the Aug 10 program began — an average of about 155 per day, not 200 — while security-force sources cited in the report said daily returns rarely exceed 100-200 and are usually just 10-20, estimating roughly 16,000 migrants remain in Ceuta versus the government's implied lower figures.

media.caption: Security sources dispute the government's claimed pace of voluntary returns from Ceuta
